answer: Timber-Origin Residency Ledger. Each agent identity must map to a physical harvest site: a registered timber parcel with GPS-tagged logs and periodic on-site audits. The enforcement rule ties transaction rights to verified cutting cycles, so one operator can only sustain identities matching parcels they actually work. A terrace registration adds a second fixed point: the processing yard where wood is dried, instrumented and inspected. Duplicate identities collapse when two claimed parcels share a mesa contour line or the same yard throughput record.
